events.title: The Old Babylonian Empire
events.description: Babylon becomes a dominant power in Mesopotamia under the First Babylonian Dynasty.

events.title: Hammurabi's Law Code
events.description: King Hammurabi of Babylon issues his famous collection of 282 laws, including the principle "an eye for an eye". One of the best-preserved law codes from antiquity.

events.title: The Middle Kingdom in Egypt
events.description: Egypt is reunified under the 11th Dynasty from Thebes. The period is regarded as a classical era for Egyptian literature and art.

events.title: Hyksos Invade Egypt
events.description: Semitic peoples called the Hyksos take control of the Nile Delta and establish the 15th Dynasty. They introduce the horse and chariot to Egypt.

events.title: Minoan Civilization on Crete
events.description: The Minoan civilization flourished on Crete with advanced palaces like Knossos, colorful frescoes, and its own writing system (Linear A).

events.title: The Mari Archives
events.description: The city of Mari by the Euphrates left behind an enormous archive of over 25,000 clay tablets that provide insight into trade, diplomacy, and daily life in Abraham's time.

events.title: The Old Hittite Kingdom
events.description: The Hittites established a powerful empire in Anatolia (modern-day Turkey) with its capital at Hattusa.

events.title: The Shang Dynasty in China
events.description: The first historically verified Chinese dynasty was established, known for its bronze ware and oracle bones featuring early Chinese script.

events.title: The Nuzi Tablets
events.description: Clay tablets from Nuzi (northeast Iraq) describe social customs similar to the patriarchal narratives: surrogate motherhood, inheritance rights, and marriage contracts.

events.title: The Ebla Archive
events.description: The city of Ebla in Syria has an archive with over 15,000 clay tablets documenting trade, politics, and religion in early Syria.
